title: OmniShotCut: Holistic Relational Shot Boundary Detection with Shot-Query Transformer
claim: Traditional detectors give uninterpretable boundaries, miss subtle discontinuities, and rely on ambiguous labels for gradual transitions.
layout: 3 panels: two on top, one wide below; film strips
description: Three rounded panels show failure modes of traditional shot boundary detection, with film-strip frame sequences as the main visual. Panel (a), top left, is 'No Relational Information'. A strip runs from a room (Shot A) through a fiery explosion transition to a room (Shot B). Blue and orange boxes below say 'Boundary Detected' with a green check, and 'Transition Type' with a red question mark and 'Dissolve? Fade? Wipe? Cut?'. A confused cartoon person sits beside them. Panel (b), top right, is 'Neglect Tiny Continuity Jump'. It shows a woman drawing, with red ovals marking the hand position. A blue arc labeled 'Discontinues' spans Shot A and Shot B at a red tick on a timeline. 'FF' markers and a short description of Sudden Jump sit underneath. Panel (c), wide at the bottom, is 'Ambiguous Transition Boundaries'. Frames f1–f14 fade from a mountain lake to a forest. A question asks which frame marks the START and which the END of the transition. An upside-down answer sits at the right.
caption: Limitations of traditional Shot Boundary Detection models. (a) Detected Shots are hard to interpret: predicted boundaries lack explicit transition semantics; (b) Sudden Jump is under-modeled and often missed; (c) Human annotations are unreliable for gradual transitions with subtle start/end frames.
abstract: Shot Boundary Detection (SBD) aims to automatically identify shot changes and divide a video into coherent shots. While SBD was widely studied in the literature, existing methods often produce non-interpretable boundaries on transitions, miss subtle yet harmful discontinuities, and rely on noisy, low-diversity annotations and outdated benchmarks. To alleviate these limitations, we propose OmniShotCut to formulate SBD as structured relational prediction, jointly estimating shot ranges with intra-shot relations and inter-shot relations, by a shot query-based dense video Transformer. To avoid imprecise manual labeling, we adopt a fully synthetic transition synthesis pipeline that automatically reproduces major transition families with precise boundaries and parameterized variants. We also introduce OmniShotCutBench, a modern wide-domain benchmark enabling holistic and diagnostic evaluation. Experiments on the benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness and generality of our method.
